KELP-FOREST SHALLOW RUINS — a clear-water sea six meters deep where the stone foundations of a coastal city form a submerged grid over four kilometers, the tallest wall-stubs rising four meters from the sandy bottom, every surface thickly colonized by kelp fronds twelve meters long waving in current.

NEEDLE-SPIRE GRANITE CLUSTER — eleven granite needles between 800 and 2200 meters tall packed within a two-kilometer radius on an otherwise flat plain, their flanks absolutely vertical for the upper half of each spire, the rock faces golden in low-angle light and black in shadow with no intermediate tone.

GLACIAL-TONGUE CLIFF ABOVE CLOUD — a glacier's terminal face hangs at the lip of a 2800-meter escarpment, its 300-meter-tall blue-green calving cliff overhanging empty air above a cloud-sea that hides the valley floor entirely, occasional ice-fall vanishing silently into the white.

ALPINE-TARNS STAIRCASE — twelve glacial lakes stacked in a staircase of hanging valleys ascending 1400 meters, each lake between 200 meters and one kilometer across, connected by waterfalls between 40 and 300 meters tall, the whole system visible from below as a silver thread on a dark rock face.

BASALT-PLATEAU CLOUD-INVERSION EDGE — a flat basalt plateau at 2700 meters ends in a sheer cliff, below which a cloud inversion layer at 1800 meters fills every valley, the plateau in clear air above while the cliff-edge appears to hang over an infinite white ocean stretching to the horizon.

SCARP-WALL HORIZON PLAIN — a perfectly flat grassless plain of compacted grey clay extending sixty kilometers to a single escarpment that rises 900 meters in an unbroken vertical face running forty kilometers east-west, the only feature in a landscape stripped of everything else by an ancient event.

RIDGE-OF-ARCHES MOUNTAIN SPINE — a mountain ridge where differential erosion has punched natural arches through five separate fins of harder rock, the arches between 30 and 150 meters tall and spaced along a three-kilometer ridgeline, each arch framing a different distant mountain range through its opening.

SUNKEN-TEMPLE JUNGLE FLOOR — a lowland jungle floor where a stone temple complex has subsided four meters below the surrounding terrain, its rooftops now level with the jungle floor, approached by descending stone staircases colonized by root-growth, the interior courtyards open wells now forty meters deep.

MONUMENTAL-STAIR PYRAMID RUIN — the largest stone pyramid on its continent, its base one kilometer square and its apex 280 meters above the jungle canopy, one entire face collapsed to expose internal chambers, the rubble of the collapse a debris field of twenty-meter stone blocks spreading two kilometers.

AQUEDUCT-SPINE PLAIN — a Roman-scale stone aqueduct system on arches between 30 and 90 meters tall runs sixty kilometers across a flat alluvial plain, its three parallel channels long dry and colonized by nesting birds, the stone bleached white by centuries of sun, some arches collapsed in twenty-meter gaps.

TITAN-WALL FORTIFICATION RUIN — a curtain wall eight meters thick and originally thirty meters tall runs for fifteen kilometers across a mountain pass, the wall now breached in a dozen places by seismic events, each breach a gap of ten to forty meters where the stone face has toppled outward.

CAVE-MOUTH GALLERY CLIFF — a limestone cliff 400 meters tall with forty-seven cave entrances between three and sixty meters wide visible on its face at various heights, each mouth exhaling cold air that condenses in thin veils, the largest cave mouth at 200 meters elevation forming a black oval eighty meters tall.

DRIPSTONE-PILLAR HALL — an underground limestone chamber one kilometer long and 200 meters wide with a ceiling 80 meters above the floor, the space filled with stalactite-stalagmite columns between two and fifteen meters in diameter, the most massive formations fused into walls dividing the space into nave-like corridors.

UNDERGROUND-SEA PHOSPHOR SHORE — a subterranean ocean whose surface glows dim blue-green from dissolved bioluminescent organisms, the ceiling 300 meters above invisible in darkness, the cave-shore a strip of grey gravel thirty meters wide between black water and a cavern wall carved smooth by ancient higher waterlines.

VOLCANIC VENT-TUBE CATHEDRAL — a lava tube fifteen meters in diameter and forty kilometers long has been breached by a surface collapse two kilometers long and 200 meters deep, the exposed tube walls showing perfect circular cross-section, lava-mark tide-lines visible in concentric rings on the inner surface.

SALT-PILLAR HYPERSALINE LAKE — a shallow inland sea deposits salt faster than evaporation removes it, building white salt pillars on the lakebed that pierce the surface by between one and six meters, five thousand pillars visible across the two-kilometer lake, each slightly translucent in low light.

STORM-ANVIL PEAK SHROUD — a 3500-meter peak maintains a permanent lenticular cloud cap extending ten kilometers downwind, the cap's underside only 200 meters above the summit, its surface smooth as a ceiling, the peak itself in eerie calm beneath a bowl of rushing cloud.

PLASMA-SPILL AURORA TUNDRA — a flat sub-arctic plain under an aurora so low and bright its green and crimson curtains appear to begin at the horizon rather than in the sky, their lower edges at 80 kilometers altitude appearing to touch the 600-meter escarpment at the plain's northern edge.

VOID-MOUTH KARST COLLAPSE — a karst landscape where a central collapse has created a circular pit 300 meters in diameter and 500 meters deep, its vertical walls showing the entire limestone stratigraphy in banded grey rings, the pit floor occupied by a lake whose depth is unknown.

CRYSTAL-CANYON GEODE RAVINE — a canyon three kilometers deep carved through a region of volcanic rock with dense geode formation, the canyon walls at every level studded with open geode pockets between one and eight meters across, the crystal interiors ranging from white quartz to deep amethyst.

ROOTWORK-BRIDGE ANCIENT GORGE — a jungle gorge 200 meters deep and sixty meters wide where the root-systems of four-meter-diameter trees on both lips have grown together across the gap over centuries, forming living bridges between one and four meters thick carrying the full weight of their host trees.

WORLD-SPINE RIFT CONVERGENCE — at the meeting of two tectonic plates a thirty-kilometer ridge of shattered and upthrust rock rises 2400 meters above the surrounding plain, the ridge too broken and jagged to call mountains, more a continuous wall of angular stone slabs each between ten and 200 meters across.

STANDING-WAVE PETRIFIED DUNE FIELD — an ancient desert's dunes turned to stone thirty million years ago, preserving the exact form of a dune-sea in red sandstone, the stone dunes between fifty and 250 meters tall with perfect slip-face angles, cross-bedding visible in every exposed cliff-face in arcing laminae.

GEOMAGNETIC STONE CIRCLE PLATEAU — a flat-topped plateau at 1200 meters ringed by a double circle of magnetic lodestone pillars each eight meters tall and two meters wide, the inner ring of forty stones and outer ring of ninety, the lodestones having deflected every compass for two hundred kilometers.

ARCHON-TOMB CLIFF NECROPOLIS — a sandstone canyon wall 800 meters tall carved over centuries into a continuous facade of tomb-entrances, the largest portals framed by columns thirty meters tall bearing eroded relief carvings, the smallest tomb-mouths only accessible by rope from ledges above, ten thousand entries total.

MOONGATE MEGALITH AVENUE — a processional avenue six kilometers long and sixty meters wide flanked by paired standing stones each twenty meters tall and spaced thirty meters apart, the avenue terminating at a trilithon arch forty meters tall whose capstone weighs an estimated four hundred tonnes.

DEEP-MANTLE WINDOW LAVA LAKE — a collapsed volcanic pit one kilometer in diameter and 700 meters deep has exposed a sustained magma lake at its floor, the pit walls a vertical stratigraphy of every lava-flow the volcano has produced in three million years, each layer a different color banded like tree-rings in stone.

PYROCLASTIC FLOW GHOST PLAIN — a hardened ash-flow deposit forty kilometers wide and perfectly flat, its surface cracked into hexagonal plates ten meters across, the far edge dissolving into a curtain of sulfurous haze where three 900-meter cinder cones rise in silhouette.

ICEFALL COLONNADE FJORD — a fjord three kilometers wide flanked by 1600-meter granite walls sheeted in vertical ice, twelve separate glacial icefalls pouring over the rim in frozen mid-cascade, each icefall between 80 and 300 meters wide and suspended 400 meters above the black water below.

CANOPY-THRONE EMERGENT GROVE — a coastal primeval forest where seven emergent trees have shed their lower branches and stand as bare columns 30 meters in diameter rising 500 meters above the continuous canopy below, their crowns isolated islands of foliage against open sky.

WIND-RIBBED SANDSTONE LABYRINTH — a canyon system cut through rose-red sandstone in parallel slots each between four and twenty meters wide and 400 meters deep, the slot walls so close at the top that only a one-meter ribbon of sky is visible from the floor, the walls smooth and rippled like frozen water.

DROWNED-ARCH TIDAL REEF COAST — a coastline where a collapsed limestone plateau has left a series of submerged arches just below the surface, the largest arch sixty meters tall and ninety meters wide, its crown two meters under water at high tide and exposed at low, barnacle-crusted and trailing kelp.

HANGING-VALLEY TWIN-SPIRE PASS — two granite needles each 2600 meters tall bracket a glacial pass at 1900 meters, the pass floor a flat snowfield one kilometer wide, the needle faces absolutely vertical and copper-stained by mineral seepage, connected by a single natural rock bridge forty meters below their summits.

ROOT-VAULTED TEMPLE SINKHOLE — a circular karst collapse 180 meters in diameter and 120 meters deep has dropped a stone temple into the earth intact, its roof now open to sky, the sinkhole walls hung with root-curtains from four-meter-diameter trees whose trunks are visible at the rim above.

GEODE-LINED MAGMA-COOLED VAULT — a vast volcanic bubble solidified at depth and later exposed by erosion forms a chamber 500 meters across, its entire interior surface armored in amethyst crystals between half a meter and six meters long, a crack in the dome floor revealing a magma channel glowing ninety meters below.

THUNDERHEAD STAIRCASE PLATEAU — a stepped sandstone plateau rising in four distinct shelves from 600 to 2100 meters, each shelf edge a sheer 300-meter drop, the highest shelf permanently capped by a stationary storm system whose base sits only fifty meters above the plateau surface.

WORLD-TREE SURFACE ROOT PLAIN — a flat basin at the base of a single tree whose trunk is eighty meters in diameter, the root system radiating outward for two kilometers in cable-thick braids between one and fifteen meters above the ground, forming a colonnaded landscape of living arches the size of cathedral naves.

ALKALI-FLAT ZIGGURAT EMERGENCE — a blinding white salt flat two hundred kilometers across broken only by the uppermost four tiers of a stone ziggurat protruding twelve meters above the crust, the structure's full height of 180 meters entombed beneath compacted mineral sediment deposited over three thousand years.

LAVA-SHELF OBSIDIAN MIRROR COAST — active lava flowing over a 600-meter coastal cliff into the sea has built a delta of cooled obsidian shelves each between twenty and sixty meters wide, their upper surfaces mirror-flat and reflecting the eruption column above, the whole coast illuminated lurid orange for ten kilometers.

FROZEN-VOID POLAR CANYON — a canyon four kilometers deep carved by a now-vanished river through polar granite, its walls coated in a two-meter skin of clear ice that preserves every crack and fissure in the original rock face, the canyon floor buried under a glacier whose surface is 3800 meters below the canyon rim.

SPORE-PILLAR BIOLUMINESCENT ABYSS — a subterranean cavern three kilometers wide and 600 meters floor-to-ceiling colonized by fungal towers between 20 and 90 meters tall, each tower pulsing amber and violet, their combined luminescence sufficient to cast sharp shadows, the ceiling invisible behind a permanent spore-cloud.

SKY-ISLAND ROOT-FALL ARCHIPELAGO — five flat-bottomed stone islands between 500 meters and three kilometers across drift at elevations between 400 and 1800 meters, root-systems from their surface vegetation hanging in curtains 200 meters below each island's rim, waterfalls arcing from their edges and evaporating before reaching ground.

ARCANE-SCAR CONFLUENCE BASIN — a bowl-shaped valley six kilometers wide where seven ley-line ridges converge at a central point, the convergence zone a circular area 300 meters in diameter where the air is visibly warped, all stone within it recrystallized to black glass, and energy filaments two meters wide arc between the surrounding ridge-crests at irregular intervals.

STORM-GLACIATED FORTRESS RIDGE — a twelve-kilometer sawtooth ridgeline at 3400 meters with the foundations of a fortress system running its entire length, the original walls now entombed in glacial ice up to forty meters thick, only the highest tower-tops and merlons protruding from the ice surface, the ridge in permanent storm-shadow.

KRAKEN-FOSSIL COASTAL ESCARPMENT — a 700-meter coastal cliff of grey limestone whose face is studded with the exposed cross-sections of fossilized cephalopods, the largest specimen a circular cross-section eight meters in diameter visible at mid-cliff height, tentacle-impressions radiating from it for twenty meters in every direction.

RUNE-SEAM MEGALITH CRATER — an ancient impact crater four kilometers in diameter and 800 meters deep whose interior walls have been carved floor-to-rim in continuous rune-script by an unknown civilization, each rune character two meters tall, the carving estimated at ninety million individual strokes, the deepest runes at the crater floor still faintly luminous.

CLOUD-SEA BASALT MONOLITH EMERGENCE — a flat basalt plain at 2200 meters sits above a permanent cloud inversion that buries everything below 1600 meters, the plain surface punctuated by forty-three freestanding basalt columns between 30 and 110 meters tall, each column's base hidden in cloud, their shafts appearing to grow from white nothing into clear amber-lit sky.
